**Summary**

I researched Apple's most recent reported results (fiscal Q4 and full fiscal year 2024, ended September 28, 2024) before deciding. From Apple's newsroom release and the FY2024 Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR: quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year (the strongest growth in several quarters, with iPhone returning to growth and Services at record levels); full-year total net sales of $391,035 million (FY2023: $383,285 million); net income of $93,736 million, or $6.08 per diluted share — depressed versus FY2023's $96,995 million/$6.13 by a one-time $10.2 billion European State Aid tax charge — and operating income of $123,216 million. With AAPL quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), the stock trades at roughly 36–37× trailing FY2024 EPS, which is a premium multiple but arguably understates normalized earnings given the tax charge, and the franchise remains highly cash-generative with a large buyback behind it. I judged the risk/reward acceptable for a modest, mandate-sized addition rather than a large commitment. I therefore placed a single buy order for 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00 — just above the touch, so still close to market — which filled at $223.00 for approximately $9,812, comfortably inside both the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, leaving the $50,000 cash balance otherwise intact and no money moved out of the account. (Note: several search-result snippets were withheld by a security screen for containing content that tried to alter my instructions or appeared to be spoofed market data; I ignored those and relied only on the Apple newsroom release, the SEC 10-K, and the broker's quote.)
